sections.h2: Where is Leavenworth, Kansas, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Leavenworth is the county seat of Leavenworth County, on the west bank of the Missouri River about 25 miles northwest of downtown Kansas City. It sits at the junction of U.S. 73 and K-92 and belongs to the Kansas City metropolitan area.

The Census Bureau lists 24.06 square miles, and Fort Leavenworth takes up the northern half of that area. Four small creeks run east through the city to the river: Quarry Creek, Corral Creek, Three Mile Creek and Five Mile Creek. Lansing lies just to the south. A house here may be a few blocks from the post, the river bluffs or one of those creek corridors, and each setting changes what a buyer will ask about drainage, grading and age.

sections.h2: What is the history of Leavenworth?
sections.html:
Leavenworth, founded in 1854, was the first city incorporated in the Kansas Territory. It grew south of Fort Leavenworth, which began in 1827 as Cantonment Leavenworth under Colonel Henry Leavenworth.

On April 3, 1858, the Leavenworth Constitution for the state of Kansas was adopted in the city, although the federal government never approved it. By 1865 the city had drawn nearly one-fifth of the 12,000 Black residents of Kansas. With a history that long, Leavenworth has many older houses, and older houses bring the usual questions about wiring, plumbing, sewer lines and foundations.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Leavenworth, and why does it matter to sellers?
sections.html:
The military is the anchor. Wikipedia reports that Fort Leavenworth employs roughly 5,600 people, making it the largest employer, followed by Leavenworth Public Schools and the Department of Veterans Affairs Eastern Kansas Health Care System.

The city's 2015 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, listed the top employers below. Treat the numbers as a snapshot from that year.

Federal and military jobs bring steady turnover. People rotate in and out of the area, and homeowners tied to those jobs can need to sell on a schedule set by someone else. That is a common reason sellers look for a quick close instead of a long listing.

sections.h2: What are Leavenworth's schools, roads and transit like?
sections.html:
Most of the city is in Leavenworth USD 453, which runs four elementary schools, one middle school and Leavenworth High School, plus a virtual school. Fort Leavenworth USD 207 covers the post, and a small southern slice of the city is in Lansing USD 469. Check which district a specific address belongs to, because buyers often ask.

Leavenworth is the largest city in Kansas without fixed-route public transit. RideLV, an app-based on-demand service run by The Guidance Center with the Kansas City Area Transportation Authority, began in April 2023. Intercity trains and buses leave from Kansas City, Missouri. Most households drive, so a house with a garage and off-street parking holds its appeal.

sections.h2: What is the weather like, and what does it mean for a Leavenworth house?
sections.html:
Leavenworth has a humid continental climate with hot, humid summers and cold, drier winters. January is on average the coldest month, July the hottest and June the wettest.

The record high is 114 F in August, and the record in May is 103 F, so roofs and air conditioners work hard. Because several creeks cross the city on their way to the river, drainage is worth checking, and buyers and inspectors often look at downspouts, grading and basement moisture. Seasonal swings between freezing winters and hot summers are also hard on masonry and foundations, and those are common items on an inspection list.

Yes. Leavenworth's Rental Registration program covers every rented single-family house, multi-family building and rented unit inside an owner-occupied dwelling. The rules are in Sections 10-568 through 10-572 of the city code.

  • Registration costs $20 per property that is titled under the same name, filed with the City Clerk at 100 N. 5th Street.
  • Properties titled under different names need separate registrations.
  • An owner who lives more than 40 miles away must name a resident agent within 40 miles, and the agent shares responsibility for upkeep and code compliance.
  • Any change in the registered information must be reported to the city in writing within 30 days.
  • Hotels, licensed bed and breakfasts, churches, nursing facilities, jails and housing authority units are exempt.

Selling a rented house changes ownership, which matters here. Because registration follows the title name, a new owner generally has to register on their own, and the old owner should notify the city of the change. Questions go to the Rental Property Coordinator at 913-364-5840.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled for Leavenworth houses?
sections.html:
Leavenworth County bills property tax, and the county treasurer collects it. Real estate taxes are paid in arrears, with the first half due by December 20 and the second half due by May 10 of the following year.

The treasurer's tax calendar says statements go out between November 1 and December 15, and that no second-half notices are sent. A seller who closes in the spring should confirm with the title company that the second half is accounted for.

The missing second-half notice trips up sellers who rely on a reminder. Missing a date means interest, and the title company will want any unpaid tax settled at closing.

sections.h2: How does deed recording work in Leavenworth County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Leavenworth houses are recorded at the Leavenworth County Register of Deeds, 300 Walnut Street, open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The office phone is 913-684-0424.

The office records warranty deeds, transfer on death deeds and quit claim deeds, among other documents. It is a recording office and cannot provide free title research. The register's site also has a property fraud page for owners. If you inherited a house and the recorded name is still the previous owner's, expect the title company to want the record cleaned up before a sale can close.

sections.h2: What are the realistic ways to sell a house in Leavenworth?
sections.html:
Sellers in Leavenworth generally choose between a listing with an agent, a sale on their own and a cash purchase.

  • A listing can bring the widest buyer pool, but a buyer's lender will require inspection items to be addressed.
  • Selling on your own works if you have time and know the disclosure and contract steps.
  • A cash offer fits houses that need work, vacant rentals, inherited houses and owners facing a deadline.

We buy houses in Leavenworth as-is, including older homes near downtown and rentals that need updates. Ask for an offer, compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, and choose the route that fits your timeline.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental in Leavenworth before selling it?
faqs.a: If the house is rented, registration is required while you own it, at $20 per property titled under the same name. When you sell, tell the city of the change within 30 days. The buyer registers separately if they rent it.

faqs.q: When are Leavenworth County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due by December 20 and the second half by May 10 of the following year. The treasurer mails statements from November 1 to December 15 and does not mail second-half notices.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Leavenworth?
faqs.a: At the Leavenworth County Register of Deeds, 300 Walnut Street in Leavenworth, 913-684-0424. The office records warranty, transfer on death and quit claim deeds.

faqs.q: Which school district covers my Leavenworth house?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Leavenworth USD 453. Fort Leavenworth USD 207 serves the post, and a small southern part of the city is in Lansing USD 469, so confirm by address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Leavenworth house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so foundation, roof or code problems do not have to be fixed before closing. A conventional buyer's lender will usually want them resolved.
